source.title: Nonuniform random feature models using derivative information
source.authors: Konstantin Pieper; Ze-Zhong Zhang; Guan-Nan Zhang

record.tranche_reason: Evaluates held-out approximation performance for random-feature shallow networks on synthetic and benchmark regression functions, extending the generalization topic to derivative-informed feature sampling. It does not test the listed claim versions directly.
record.gate_note: The study compares test/validation approximation errors for uniform, derivative-informed, active-subspace, residual-based, and sparse feature methods. It does not test random-label memorization, the listed image-architecture or optimizer comparisons, dropout, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Numerical results appear in figures; cited prior-work results are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study compares derivative-informed feature sampling methods for regularized shallow-network regression. None of its results tests V1–V8. In particular, error curves against feature count do not establish continued generalization beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold (V2). It cites the V2 original for its theoretical framework, without testing or using that finding.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's conclusion is substantially accurate: derivative-informed nonuniform sampling can narrow the approximation-efficiency gap between uniform random features and fully trained sparse networks, with explicit structural failure cases. Qualify the evaluation: regularization is selected using validation data, and reported approximation error is evaluated on training plus validation data, rather than an independent held-out test set.
record.recipe_differences: Shallow random-feature regression with fixed sampled inner weights and least-squares-trained outer weights; synthetic and benchmark regression tasks, rather than the classification, optimizer, architecture, regularization, or memorization procedures in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Function structure and sampling strategy change outcomes: globally anisotropic functions favor active-subspace sampling; local anisotropy favors localized gradient methods; simple gradient sampling can stagnate on nonsmooth or separable functions. The nonlocal method uses δW = 2δ in the reported general setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Derivative-informed sampling improves regression approximation over uniform sampling in several settings, with benefits depending on function structure. Global active-subspace sampling misses local anisotropy, and simple gradient sampling can stagnate or miss separable structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested regularized shallow regression models, derivative-informed feature sampling can reduce approximation error at a given feature count when its directional and spatial assumptions match the target function.

record.problems: The reported comparisons are primarily shown in figures without numerical values in the text; uncertainty intervals or statistical tests are not stated. The examples are regression tasks, many synthetic, and do not evaluate classification or random-label memorization.
record.rows_left_out: No separately stated result with an explicit outcome was omitted. Figures 5–11 contain additional method curves; where the supplied text gives no method-specific outcome beyond the plotted result, no row is reconstructed from the figure alone.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and their coexistence under the same architecture and recipe.
Test-error behavior beyond a demonstrated width sufficient for zero training error under training without explicit regularization.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization and dependence on tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random removal and measuring retrained test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures address a different question. They do not signify that the reported sampling comparisons are unreadable. No additional result bearing on a listed version was found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; CIFAR-10/ImageNet classification.
Test error as width increases past interpolation on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large-batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout effects and interaction with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with train-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.note: The integral formula and residual-based method are separately said to outperform uniform sampling by a small margin; the figure is not numerically transcribed.
rows.check: No version applies. Split nonlocal and residual sampling: the text first describes both as roughly matching uniform sampling, then specifically reports a small advantage for residual sampling and the integral formula. The combined absent state loses that distinction.
